label: Keeled Scales
description: Will Johnson (Centro-matic, South San Gabriel, Monsters of Folk) sings in a craggy, weathered rasp over spare, atmospheric folk-rock built from acoustic guitar, brushed drums and low organ drones. It is unhurried, private-feeling songwriting, closer to a late-night confession than a rock record.
lineage: Johnson's solo work extends the Secretly Canadian/Jason Molina-adjacent lineage of haunted, Crazy Horse-scaled Americana into a quieter solo register.
borderline_note: Placed in V1 (named in that lane's own definition as part of the Will Johnson orbit) with C2 as secondary for its barroom-storyteller feel.

label: Keeled Scales
description: A hushed, largely solo-recorded set named for the Spanish Civil War and other historical fragments, matching Johnson's plainspoken baritone to spare guitar and occasional strings. It sits at the quiet, wounded end of his catalog.
lineage: Continues the same Molina/Centro-matic-adjacent lineage as Johnson's other solo records.

label: Keeled Scales
description: Desert-toned cosmic country from an Austin band steeped in Marfa mysticism: reverb-heavy pedal steel, loping tempos and Shannon's high, reedy voice drifting over slow-building arrangements.
lineage: Part of the 2010s Austin cosmic-country revival alongside Twain and Promised Land Sound, drawing on Gram Parsons-style country rock filtered through desert psychedelia.

label: Keeled Scales
description: Three-song EP of slow-motion, synth-tinged dream-folk from Carly Bond's San Francisco project: sparse arrangements, cavernous reverb and a fragile, close-mic'd vocal at the center.
lineage: Extends Meernaa's hushed, slowcore-adjacent songwriting between Duster-style haze and modern indie folk.

label: Keeled Scales
description: Mat Davidson's twain project sets a high, keening voice against loose, fingerpicked country-folk with occasional bursts of full-band warmth. It's intimate cosmic country, closer to a campfire than a road trip.
lineage: Davidson's songwriting draws directly on Gram Parsons-style cosmic country and old-time singing, filtered through a DIY, small-label folk scene.

label: Keeled Scales
description: A warmer, more full-band twain record than its predecessors, still built around Davidson's reedy tenor but adding lightly psychedelic guitar textures and looser tempos.
lineage: Continues the cosmic-country lineage of Rare Feeling with a slightly fuller studio palette.

label: Keeled Scales
description: Why Bonnie's debut full-length trades their earlier bedroom dream-pop for raw-edged, feedback-streaked indie rock; frontwoman Blair Howerton has cited Townes Van Zandt and Blaze Foley alongside the Replacements and Sparklehorse as touchstones for its road-trip-through-Texas songwriting.
lineage: A Texas band's move from dream pop toward a more country-and-alt-rock-inflected sound, echoing the wider indie-twang turn without being a straight country record.
borderline_note: Primarily a slacker/indie-rock record; C1 given as secondary for its explicit Townes Van Zandt/Blaze Foley-referencing songwriting and Texas road-song content.

label: Keeled Scales
description: Hushed, minor-key indie folk built from finger-picked guitar and Lucille's airy, wavering voice, with lyrics circling grief and the underworld (the title nods to Persephone's myth).
lineage: Sits in the 2010s Austin/Bandcamp indie-folk scene alongside labelmates Rae Fitzgerald and Erin Durant.

label: Keeled Scales
description: A dreamy, lo-fi debut from a Louisiana songwriter working partly in French, mixing Cajun-inflected folk melody with woozy, four-track-style production.
lineage: Draws on South Louisiana's French-language folk tradition filtered through a hushed, Bandcamp-era indie-folk sensibility.

label: Keeled Scales
description: Piano-led songs from a former touring keyboardist (Jenny Lewis, Phosphorescent) stepping into her own material: slow-building, emotionally direct arrangements built around Schornikow's plainspoken alto.
lineage: A session-musician's turn to solo songwriting, closer in spirit to the piano-based end of indie folk/slowcore than to any single scene.

label: Keeled Scales
description: Jazzy, warm-toned folk from a New Orleans songwriter, mixing loose acoustic guitar and piano with unhurried melodic turns that owe as much to Randy Newman as to any folk revivalist.
lineage: Grows out of Durant's New Orleans singer-songwriter background before her later, more country-facing Ruination Record Co. records.

label: Tell 'Em Tapes
description: A six-song, lo-fi indie-folk EP of intimate, close-mic'd acoustic songs from an Austin songwriter later signed to Keeled Scales.
lineage: Part of the same Austin DIY-folk circle as Julia Lucille and RF Shannon.
borderline_note: Found via the Keeled Scales catalog (a later home for the artist); this earlier EP itself was released on Tell 'Em Tapes, confirmed on its own Bandcamp page.

label: Dear Life Records
description: A 28-track compilation of Aaron Dowdy's earliest home-recorded songs (2017-2018), released as a single sprawling document years before Fust became a full band. Rough four-track country songs, drum-machine and all, that show the roots of the band's later, more polished storytelling.
lineage: Predates and directly seeds the full-band Fust sound heard on Genevieve and Big Ugly; a look at the songwriter's home-recording origins before the Dear Life Records band era.
borderline_note: A compilation of early home-recorded EPs rather than a single planned album; included as a documented prequel to Fust's later, already-staged LPs.

label: Dear Life Records
description: A shifting North Carolina old-time/DIY-noise collective (members of Sluice and Magic Tuber Stringband among them) recording traditional ballads and hymns with tape manipulation and found-sound production, cut live at a family dairy farm in Virginia.
lineage: Bridges the Piedmont old-time/string-band tradition with the same DIY network that produces Sluice and Fust, treating inherited folk songs as raw material for experimental production.
borderline_note: Closer to experimental old-time/noise than to the twang-rock core of C5; kept here for its Dear Life/Sluice ties, with V8 (American Primitive/drone folk) as secondary.

label: Dear Life Records
description: Michael Cormier-O'Leary's chamber-folk ensemble Hour expands to a 13-piece orchestra of winds, strings and vibraphone for a slow, meditative suite about disappearance and loss, closer to instrumental chamber music than a rock record.
lineage: Cormier-O'Leary also founded Dear Life Records and plays in Friendship and 2nd Grade, tying Hour directly into the same Philadelphia deadpan/slowcore circle.
borderline_note: Mostly instrumental chamber-folk rather than twang; included under C8's hushed/sparse definition for its Dear Life/Cormier-O'Leary lineage.

label: Dear Life Records
description: A 15-track live album stitched together from two years of DIY touring, capturing Hour's shifting chamber-folk ensemble across bars, movie theaters and living rooms.
lineage: A touring-diary capstone to Hour's catalog before Ghost Bridge, part of the same Dear Life Records/Cormier-O'Leary world as Friendship and 2nd Grade.

label: Lame-O Records
description: Dave Benton's Trace Mountains project leans further into pedal-steel-flecked, warmly recorded country-pop on this record, mixing jangling guitars with synths and unhurried melodies.
lineage: A former LVL UP member's move toward twangier, more countryish songwriting, part of the same Brooklyn/Lame-O indie scene as Slaughter Beach, Dog.

label: Lame-O Records
description: Matt Scottoline's Hurry project debut: tight, hook-forward power pop with an easy, unfussy jangle, plainspoken lyrics about heartbreak and self-doubt.
lineage: Part of the same Philadelphia power-pop revival as 2nd Grade and Golden Apples, descended from Big Star and Superchunk.

label: Lame-O Records
description: A sprawling 20-song double set of concise, hook-driven power pop split into 'Girls' and 'Boys' halves, led by Peter Gill (also of Friendship and Hour).
lineage: Continues 2nd Grade's Big Star/Guided by Voices-indebted songwriting within the same Dear Life/Lame-O Philadelphia scene as Friendship and Hurry.

label: Lame-O Records
description: A brief, three-song burst of ringing, mid-fi guitar pop from another corner of Lame-O's Philadelphia power-pop stable, all hooks and no filler in under seven minutes total.
lineage: Part of the same Philadelphia jangle-pop scene as Hurry and 2nd Grade.

label: Alive Naturalsound Records
description: A laid-back homage to '70s Topanga Canyon and Marin County sounds from a band built around former Beachwood Sparks players: jangly, country-tinged FM rock full of easy harmonies.
lineage: Formed by Beachwood Sparks/Jonny Niemann/Neal Casal alumni, directly continuing the Paisley Underground-to-cosmic-country lineage that Curation Records now catalogs.

label: Curation
description: The Paisley Underground/cosmic-country pioneers' first album in over a decade, mixing pedal-steel-laced country rock with the band's longtime cosmic, harmony-driven sound.
lineage: A late-career return from one of the foundational 2000s cosmic-country/Paisley Underground revival bands (V15/C6's direct lineage), now released on their own reissue-and-new-music label.
borderline_note: Band's classic-era catalog (2000-2012) is V-zone Paisley Underground territory; this 2024 record alone is Core-era and staged here.

label: Paradise of Bachelors
description: A young Nashville band's second album, expanding from garage-country burners into ambitious, Byrds/Big Star-indebted psych-country with guest guitar from Steve Gunn.
lineage: Nashville's 2010s cosmic-country underground, tied to Paradise of Bachelors' wider American-vernacular roster and to Steve Gunn's Black Dirt Studio circle.

label: Paradise of Bachelors
description: Erin Birgy's surrealist song-world turns painterly and desert-lit on this record, co-produced with Big Thief's James Krivchenia: avant-pop arrangements wrapped around plainspoken, image-dense lyrics.
lineage: Connected to the Big Thief/indie-folk network via Krivchenia's production; sits at the arty edge of the twangy indie-folk lane.
borderline_note: More art-pop than twang; included as a borderline C5 fit given its acoustic-folk backbone and Big Thief-circle production ties.

label: Paradise of Bachelors
description: A Halifax band's third album of loose, literate slacker rock: ringing guitars, unhurried tempos and Nigel Chapman's plainspoken, philosophically digressive vocal delivery.
lineage: Explicitly indebted to Pavement, the Clean, the Go-Betweens and Silver Jews-style deadpan songwriting, making Nap Eyes a direct continuation of the C7 slacker/jangle lineage.

label: Orindal Records
description: Owen Ashworth's post-Casiotone project sets deadpan, plainly sung short stories about Michigan, Christmas, and lost people over minimal drum machine and synth, calling PopMatters' Indie Pop Album of the Year in 2015.
lineage: A direct continuation of the Drag City deadpan school through Ashworth's own Orindal Records, feeding the same lineage as Silver Jews and Advance Base's Casiotone predecessor.

label: Orindal Records
description: Friendship frontman Dan Wriggins' solo debut EP: minimal, open-frame production (organ, quiet drums, classical guitar) behind fragmentary, prose-poem lyrics delivered in a solemn, wounded voice.
lineage: Wriggins cites Kath Bloom and Vic Chesnutt as models; a direct extension of his alt-country band Friendship's deadpan storytelling into a solo, more skeletal form.

label: Orindal Records
description: A Chicago multi-instrumentalist's (Ohmme, Marker) solo debut: spare piano- and violin-inflected songs recorded mostly alone, moving between chamber-folk intimacy and quiet dissonance.
lineage: Grows out of Chicago's overlapping indie-folk/experimental scene, tied to Orindal labelmates Gia Margaret and Macie Stewart's other Chicago projects.

label: Dalliance Recordings
description: A hushed, lo-fi debut of whispery vocals over sparse acoustic guitar and piano, later reissued via the Orindal Records-adjacent Chicago scene.
lineage: Sits alongside Chicago's Orindal/Dear Nora/Advance Base circle of quiet, home-recorded songwriting.
borderline_note: Original label is Dalliance Recordings, not Orindal; discovered via the Orindal catalog page, year/label confirmed on the artist's own Bandcamp page.

label: Keeled Scales / Orindal Records
description: A Tucson artist's solo-produced record blending Americana-tinged songwriting with ambient sound design: synthesizer, tape loops, field recordings and her own desert-referencing lyrics.
lineage: A joint release between Keeled Scales and Orindal Records, connecting Tucson's desert-folk scene to both labels' networks.

label: Ruination Record Co.
description: Durant's most recent record continues her warm, jazz-inflected folk songwriting, now on the Brooklyn label Ruination Record Co.
lineage: A later-career continuation of the same New Orleans folk songwriting heard on her earlier Keeled Scales record Islands.

label: Ruination Record Co.
description: Dan Knishkowy's Adeline Hotel project offers gentle, fingerpicked indie folk with plainspoken, slightly wry lyrics about memory and routine.
lineage: Part of a small Brooklyn/Ruination songwriter circle (Frank Meadows, Jackie West, The Bird Calls) that frequently collaborates across each other's records.

label: Ruination Record Co.
description: A piano-led, songs-first country record from the Fust bassist and Dear Life Records co-owner, mixing Neil Young-style keyboard balladry with Lambchop-esque narrative turns and field-recording interludes.
lineage: Meadows co-runs Dear Life Records and plays in Fust, linking this solo record directly to that North Carolina/Brooklyn alt-country network.

label: Ruination Record Co.
description: A Brooklyn songwriter's guitar-and-synth indie rock record, made with a rotating cast from the same Ruination/Adeline Hotel circle (Dan Knishkowy, Katie Von Scheicher).
lineage: Part of the same small Brooklyn songwriter-collaborator scene as Adeline Hotel, Office Culture and The Bird Calls.

label: Ruination Record Co.
description: Sam Sodomsky's songwriting project draws explicit comparison to David Berman, John Darnielle and Destroyer's Dan Bejar: clever, plainspoken songs balancing folksy earnestness against wry self-awareness.
lineage: A direct continuation of the Drag City deadpan-songwriter lineage (Berman, Darnielle) within the small Brooklyn Ruination/Adeline Hotel circle.
key_tracks: To Everything There Is A Ceiling

label: Polyvinyl
description: Ella Williams's fourth Squirrel Flower album is dense, expansive guitar rock about work, anxiety and climate dread, cut with Alex Farrar (MJ Lenderman, Wednesday) and players from Wednesday, Bon Iver and the War on Drugs.
lineage: Farrar's production ties Squirrel Flower directly into the Asheville Drop of Sun network that also produced Wednesday and MJ Lenderman.
borderline_note: Straighter indie rock than most of C1, but included for its direct Alex Farrar/Wednesday-circle production credits.

album: Say a Prayer to the Gods of Getting Going
label: Polyvinyl
description: A travel-inspired record balancing Williams's enveloping voice against crunchy, wall-of-guitar live production, drawing comparisons to Wednesday and Alex G.
lineage: Continues Squirrel Flower's move toward the countrygaze-adjacent, guitar-wall sound of Wednesday's circle.
